stories.headline: test3's Gibbs-White Fielding Fresh Interest
stories.deck: Spurs gossip circles Gibbs-White, owned by test3, with Gabriel and White also in Monday's talk
stories.body:
Monday's gossip lands on three names already on rolls in this league. Gibbs-White, test3's man, sits at the centre of a reported Spurs move worth a figure that would make anyone's ownership feel provisional. Nothing is settled, and until it is, test3 keeps him.

Around the same column, test31121's Gabriel has his next step unresolved and test3331 owns White. The wire offers no dates, no fees confirmed, no line-ups. What is known is that three managers here are watching the same speculation the rest of us are, and holding their assets until it hardens into fact.

stories.headline: Semenyo Sends test2 Home Empty
stories.deck: test1 beat test2 39-34, Semenyo's 13 the top score in the tie
stories.body:
Semenyo settled this. Thirteen from the forward gave test1 a total nobody in test2's line-up could match, and around him Kelleher and Wirtz added six apiece to hold the five-point margin. A goalkeeper's clean tally and a midfielder pulling his weight; the rest of test1's outfield did little, but they did not need to.

test2 will look up top and wince. A four-man forward line of Cunha, Isak, Havertz and Havertz's fellow strikers returned six, five and two, nineteen between them where one Semenyo did thirteen. Hall's eight from defence was the best test2 had, Trafford's seven behind him, and the front pay never repaid the faith.

Cunha and Isak, two points apart again, is the story that keeps not ending. test2 needed a haul from one of them and got a pair of quiet afternoons. Five points is a Semenyo, and test2 did not have one.

stories.headline: Groß National Product Powers 123 Past test4
stories.deck: 123 beat test4 38-27, Groß's eleven the top score of the tie
stories.body:
Groß settled it. Eleven for 123's midfielder was the highest score on either side, and Schade's eight behind him gave 123 a top pair test4 never came close to matching. Haaland's six and threes from Horníček and Stach padded the total to 38, comfortable in the end.

Cherki carried test4 as far as one man could, his seven the only return worth the name. Justin's six from defence backed him, but the drop after that was a cliff. E.Le Fée managed five, and then the floor gave way.

Gray, Mbeumo and N.Williams returned two apiece, six points from three men who were meant to do more. That is where the eleven-point margin lives. Cherki and Justin did their part; nobody else in test4's line-up got out of second gear.

stories.headline: Kostoulas Greeks Out A Winner For test31121
stories.deck: test31121 beat test3 30-24, Kostoulas top-scoring on eight as the deadlocked tie finally broke
stories.body:
A tie that sat at nil for so long ended with test31121 six clear, and Kostoulas carried it. His eight up top led every man on the page, and the two defenders behind him did the rest of the work: Ampadu six, Botman two. A back line that scores is a back line that wins ties.

test3 had the round's other standout in Pickford, seven from a goalkeeper and the sort of return that ought to anchor a week. It did not. Ndiaye's five was the only other outfield contribution worth the name; Emersonn, Gibbs-White and Gonzalo mustered two apiece and Grimes three, and that is not enough behind a single seven.

test31121's midfield offered nothing either, Berge on three, Ødegaard and Petrović on two, but they did not need it. The defenders and the forward had already settled it, and test3's forwards blanking short is what will sting.

stories.headline: Ajer And Thomas Wall Off test211
stories.deck: test3331 beat test211 23-16, Ajer and Thomas six apiece from the back
stories.body:
It was the defence that carried test3331 home. Ajer and Thomas took six each, Leno added three behind them, and a back line worth fifteen was more than test211's whole side could manage. The 23-16 margin was built where test3331 spent least and got most.

Lewis-Potter and Scott chipped a fortnight's worth of nothing into meaningful numbers only in the sense that they were there, both on two, Barkley a lone point. This was not a forward's win. It was a clean sheet doing the talking and the rest arriving as change.

test211 will look at Bogle's five and see the one man who turned up. Damsgaard managed three, then Clarke, Enciso, Gakpo and King all stalled on two, a midfield and a forward line queuing up to blank in tandem. Six players, sixteen points, and not one of them past the halfway mark of what Ajer alone returned.

That is the annoyance in it. test211 needed a haul from somewhere and got a spread of twos, while test3331 asked their defenders for a night's work and were repaid double.

stories.headline: Tarkowski Digs In, test31 Dug Out
stories.deck: testf beat test31 48-38, Tarkowski's defensive nine the top score.
stories.body:
testf leaned on the back and got a spine. Tarkowski's nine led the ledger from defence, De Cuyper adding five alongside him, and the midfield pair of Barnes on eight and Willock on seven did the rest. Tzolakis chipped a clean six in goal. Forty-eight, built without a forward doing much of anything.

N.Angulo managed four at the sharp end, and testf did not need more. The damage was done further back.

test31 had Buendía top the side on seven and Barry on six up front, Verbruggen matching Tzolakis with six of his own. That was the tie's competitive half. Below it, the wheels: Mykolenko five, Belloumi four, and Bobb marooned on three in midfield.

Thirty-eight is what a thin bottom half gets you. test31 will look at Bobb and Belloumi, nine between them, and know the ten-point gap sat there all along.

stories.headline: Cunha Deflects Fulham's Best-Laid Plans
stories.deck: Cunha's 89th-minute deflected strike earns United a point and hands test2 a late forward return.
stories.body:
The deflection went in for test2. Cunha's strike deep into stoppage carried United to a point at Fulham, and the fortune it needed off a body in front of goal counts the same on test2's sheet as anything struck sweetly. A late forward return, salvaged from a match that was drifting away from him.

That it kept Fulham from a first league win of the season is the wire's story, not ours. What matters here is timing: Cunha found his return in the 89th minute or not at all, and for test2 that is the difference between a blank up top and a haul that arrived when there was almost nothing left to arrive.

stories.headline: Isak Repays test2 On Iraola's Homecoming
stories.deck: Isak's second-half winner in Liverpool's 1-0 at Bournemouth returns for owner test2.
stories.body:
One goal settled it and it belonged to test2. Isak's second-half strike carried Liverpool to a narrow win, and the return lands with the manager who already carries Cunha up top.

The wire gives the goal and little else. A single forward return, no more and no less, and for test2 it is another week where the front pair does the talking.

stories.headline: Cunha Late, test2 Not Waiting
stories.deck: Cunha's last-minute equaliser for Man Utd hands test2 a return, though his week up top stayed thin
stories.body:
Cunha found it at the death for Manchester United, and test2 take a forward return from a fixture that had given them nothing to hold. It is the sort of point that arrives after the ledger looks closed, when a manager has already made peace with the blank.

That it lands late is little comfort against the shape of test2's week up front. The return steadies Cunha's line; it does not repair the pairing that has run two apart all week. What is known is the goal and the return. Everything beyond that test2 will wait for.

stories.headline: Barcelona Circle 123's Norwegian Number Nine
stories.deck: Wire links Barcelona to Haaland (owned by 123) and holds Wirtz (test1) at Liverpool for now.
stories.body:
The gossip pages put a large Barcelona offer against Haaland's name, and Haaland is 123's. Nothing is settled and nothing is signed. But a January move for a forward carrying this much of a squad is the kind of line 123 reads twice.

For test1 the wire runs the other way. Liverpool are said to be holding firm on Wirtz, so test1's man stays where he is with no date on any of it. Known for now, and no more than that.

stories.headline: Brown Says A Word, Scott Says Nothing
stories.deck: Scott, owned by test3331, gets a mention in a Celtic-Rangers preview that carries no draft weight.
stories.body:
Scott Brown holds forth on Sunday's derby, and somewhere in the copy sits the name test3331 will care about. Scott is on those rolls, and a big Old Firm afternoon is the sort that reads across to a fantasy owner watching from a distance.

What the wire gives is a preview and a former captain's verdict, no more. No line-up, no minutes, no fitness note attached to Scott. test3331 knows the fixture is coming and knows nothing beyond it, and neither do we.

stories.headline: Rushworth Keeps Goal And His Manager Guessing
stories.deck: Semenyo's two goals and an assist top the team of the week; Rushworth benched by test211 despite a clean sheet, an assist and two saves.
stories.body:
Semenyo is the man of the week and there is no argument in it. Two goals and an assist across the ninety, a forward doing the forward's job and then some, and test1 carried on his back. When a striker returns the full set nobody else in the eleven touches him.

The back is thin by design in a 1-2-5-3, so both defenders had to earn it and both did. Hall got on the scoresheet for test2, a goal from the back that no manager complains about, while Tarkowski added the assist and the clean sheet for testf and asked no questions. Behind them Rushworth is the story of the side. An assist, a clean sheet and two saves in goal, and his own manager at test211 left him on the bench. You do not often see a keeper post that line and watch it count for nothing at home.

The middle is where the side is built, five across it and every man returning. Groß was the pick, a goal and an assist and a clean sheet for 123, the complete midfield week. Barnes matched the creativity with two assists for testf and Willock found the net, so testf carry three of this eleven and would carry more on another week. Wirtz kept the assist and the sheet for test1, and Gomez did the same for test31, another man his manager sat down and another who made him regret it.

Up front Schade is the outlier, two assists and a clean sheet from a forward berth, a creator playing the point for 123. Kostoulas gave test31121 a goal and an assist and kept it tidy at the other end too. It is a front three that fetched and carried as much as it finished.

Unlucky to miss is a hard case to make against a side this full, but a fourth testf man would not have shamed anybody. The shape is the real tell: two at the back, five in the middle, and the week decided by midfielders who would not stop scoring.

And finally, a word about the men left on their own benches. Rushworth and Gomez both returned clean sheets and assists from the seats their managers chose, and they join a lengthening list this league keeps compiling. Davis, Gvardiol and Yalcouyé last time, these two now. At some point the benching stops being bad luck and starts being a habit worth naming.

stories.headline: test1 Top Of A Crowded Middle
stories.deck: test1 alone at the summit on 12; a logjam of five sides on nine and six behind them, test4 propping up the table.
stories.body:
One side has separated. test1 stand alone on 12 and their 203 is not a fluke of a soft fixture list; the win over test2 was earned by five and the only blemish came against a side few will fancy carrying forward. Behind them the middle is a scrum, four managers on nine points and daylight between what they scored and what the table says they are.

The pretenders are easy to find. testf sit second and have the ceiling to prove it, 234 the highest in the league. test2 lost yet outscore three of the sides above them in the table, and their 196 says more than nine points does. At the foot, test4 have one win and a season of trading that has not moved them; 123 beat them by eleven and remain the better argument despite matching points. Nobody below sixth is fooling this desk.

ranks.line: Alone at the top and it is no accident; the only side that has strung it together.
The highest score in the league belongs to test2's chasers, and 234 is not luck; better than second.
Lost by five and still outscoring most of the middle; the table flatters everyone but them.
Three wins and 190 is honest work, but the loss to test3331 exposed how thin the margins are.
Fifth on nine points with the lowest haul of anyone at that mark; running on fumes.
Six points undersells them; 203 scored is level with test1 and the beating of test4 was comprehensive.
Beat test3 to keep the lights on, but a flat midfield keeps costing them and 162 tells the tale.
Chased testf's lead and fell ten short; the returns are not there and 174 confirms it.
A win over test211 papers over the lowest score in the league; the outfield is not firing.
One win, all the trading in the league, and nothing to show; the dealing has not saved them.

stories.headline: test31121 Left The Clean Sheets Outside
stories.deck: test31121 sat A.Becker and Gvardiol, both returned; Rushworth, Gomez and Branthwaite also left out by their managers this week.
stories.body:
test31121 dressed a defence and then left two of its best out. A.Becker kept a clean sheet with two saves across the ninety, and Gvardiol added an assist. Both worked from a bench their manager chose, which is the cruellest sort of clean sheet a keeper can keep.

test31 matched the trick. Gomez took an assist and a clean sheet inside eighty-five minutes, and A.Becker was not even the only goalkeeper left cooling his heels this week. That title also belonged to test211, who sat Rushworth for an assist, a clean sheet and two saves over the full ninety.

test1 completed the set with Branthwaite, ninety minutes and a clean sheet, watched rather than fielded. Five men did their jobs. Not one of them counted for the manager who owned him.

stories.headline: Gvardiol Backs Himself At Left-Back
stories.deck: test31121's Gvardiol reported returning to his best at left-back for City after an injury-hit spell
stories.body:
The wire has Josko Gvardiol trending back towards his best, the left-sided defender central to a strong City start after injury wrecked the back end of his last campaign. For test31121, the reading is simple enough: a defender on the rolls looks fit and looks trusted.

No return date is attached because none is needed here. He is playing, and that is the point. test31121's back line has carried enough uncertainty this season without one of its better names in doubt.

stories.headline: Barry Good Return For test31
stories.deck: Barry's goal for Everton over 10-man Ipswich lands in test31's column.
stories.body:
Everton go unbeaten again, fifth in the table, and Thierno Barry supplies the goal that settles it against ten men. For test31 that is the return, and it lands with testf's two-point lead still to be answered.

One strike, one owner. test31 needed the front men to fire in that chase, and Barry is the one who has.

stories.headline: Suzuki Fills The Gap For test4
stories.deck: Suzuki keeps goal in Villa's first win; Martinez, owned by test3331, watches on.
stories.body:
The Villa goal has changed hands, and so has the draft value in it. Zion Suzuki, on test4's rolls, kept a clean sheet as Villa took their first league win of the season at Tottenham. For a manager already leaning on his newest men to close a hole, a goalkeeper delivering in the fixture is the answer test4 needed.

For test3331 it is the other side of the same coin. Emiliano Martinez, still owned here, no longer holds the position, and the wire does not say when or whether that changes. What is known is that the return came from the man in the sticks, and the man in the sticks belongs to somebody else.

stories.headline: Suzuki Motors test4 Forward
stories.deck: test4's Suzuki keeps goal in Villa's 3-2 win at Spurs, a plus for test4 against 123
stories.body:
Zion Suzuki kept goal in Villa's 3-2 win at Tottenham, and Emery singled him out afterwards. He is test4's man, and test4 is the one manager who needs a name to answer this week.

A winning goalkeeper who draws his manager's praise is the return test4 was chasing against 123. What the line reads is not yet ours to print, only that Suzuki was on the right side of a five-goal match and named for it.

stories.headline: Pedro Out, test211 Short Up Front
stories.deck: João Pedro, owned by test211, ruled out through injury with no return date given
stories.body:
João Pedro is out injured, and test211 lose the forward without a line on how long. The wire has Chelsea unable to score without him, which is the part that matters here: a striker on the treatment table is a striker returning nothing until he is fit.

No timeframe has been given, so none is offered. test211's defenders have already been doing the heavy lifting week to week, and now they do it a man light at the sharp end.

stories.headline: Gabriel Blows In A Catalan Wind
stories.deck: test31121's teenager JJ Gabriel travels to Barcelona as Europe's biggest clubs chase his signature.
stories.body:
The clubs circling JJ Gabriel are not test31121's problem yet, but they are test31121's asset. The 15-year-old has travelled to Barcelona while the biggest names in Europe queue for a signature, and the manager who holds him on this league's rolls watches the same reports as the rest of us.

Nothing has changed on paper. Gabriel is still test31121's, no minutes attach to any of it, and there is nothing to act on. But a squad that has already given its owner a flat midfield and a selection headache now has a name whose next move belongs to somebody else entirely.

stories.headline: Two Deals, No Rush, Same Old Story
stories.deck: Only two moves in the window, nobody churning, Raya still unclaimed.
stories.body:
Two deals in the window. Call it what it is: a quiet week, quieter than the last if that were possible, and the last was already a morgue.

test4 did their one piece of business the honest way, one in and one out, the only manager in the league to trade rather than merely add. test31 and testf each took a single name and gave up nothing. That is the whole of it. Nobody is churning, nobody is turning over a squad, and the waiver wire has the traffic of a Sunday morning.

David Raya remains where he was left. Signed in hope, dropped without ceremony, survived by a bench spot. The league has walked past him five times now and shows no sign of stooping.

Which is the trend, such as it is: the men the league keeps passing around are the men nobody wants twice. Two deals do not make a market.

quiz.q: How many deals went through the window this week?
Which manager was the only one to move a player out?
Which two managers added a player without dropping one?

stories.headline: test1 shades it as test4 draws blanks
stories.deck: test1 beat test4 38-11, Calvert-Lewin's eight the top score
stories.body:
Nothing worked for test4 and nothing came close. Eleven points across six men, not one of them past three, and the whole afternoon summed up by Gray's three at the top of the pile. Mbeumo two, Suzuki two, Justin two, N.Williams two, Cherki one. A ceiling that low loses to most totals and lost to this one by 27.

test1 needed no heroics and got a spread anyway. Calvert-Lewin's eight led it, Guéhi and Saka each returned six from opposite ends of the pitch, and Palmer's five kept the middle ticking over. Kelleher and Wirtz added three apiece and the thing was settled long before the maths got interesting.

What will gnaw at test4 is the absence of a single haul to hang the week on. Everyone contributed a little; nobody contributed enough. When your best forward returns two, the arithmetic is unkind before you start.

stories.headline: Dunk done: test3 sinks test2
stories.deck: test3 beat test2 46-21, Dunk's twelve from the back the top score
stories.body:
A defender fronted this one. Dunk's twelve settled it long before the forwards were counted, and Calafiori's six behind him meant test3 took eighteen from two men filed in defence. Emersonn's nine gave the top of the sheet the weight the back of it did not need.

Pickford's six for the clean sheet and Gibbs-White's five rounded a total that never looked like slipping. Only Gonzalo, on two, kept quiet.

test2 had nothing to answer with. Rice's six was the best of it and everything after fell away, Giles on four, Trafford on three from goal, Cunha and Isak on two apiece. Two forwards for four points is the line that will gnaw at him.

Twenty-five is a hammering, and it was built where test2 will least have expected it, in the two defensive slots that carried eighteen on their own.

stories.headline: Groß national product carries 123 39
stories.deck: 123 39 edge test211 40-39, Groß's 14 the top score
stories.body:
Fourteen from Groß did the settling. The midfielder was the biggest number on either side, and 123 39 needed every point of him, because behind that the returns thinned fast. Schade added ten up front, Haaland six, and a one-point win was built on the pair at the top and little else.

The floor is where 123 39 will look with relief. Stach three, B.Fernandes two, Neto two. Slim contributions, but in a margin of one they all counted.

test211 lost this by a single point and the defence is what will gnaw. Bogle led the side with twelve, Castagne added six, Aina two, three defenders returning and still not enough. João Pedro's nine up front was honest work with nobody alongside him, King and Enciso managing two apiece. One more point anywhere and the tie flips.
